questions.text: Access uses least-privilege identities and roles; no shared long-lived credentials.
Data is encrypted at rest and in transit with managed keys.
Threat detection and audit logging are enabled and centralized.
Incident response runbooks exist, with an owner and an alert route.
Automated backups cover every stateful component and restores are tested.
A disaster recovery plan defines RTO and RPO and is exercised.
Critical paths span multiple zones; no single point of failure.
Infrastructure is defined as code and deployed through CI/CD.
Metrics, logs and alerts cover each component with defined SLOs.
Services are right-sized for the workload and reviewed periodically.
Scaling and caching are used where load is variable or read-heavy.
Resources are tagged and budgets with alerts exist per environment.
Storage lifecycle and tiering policies remove unneeded data and compute.
